questions.text:
Consider a database that has the relation schemas EMP(EmpId, EmpName, DepId) and DEPT(DeptName, DeptId). Note that the DeptId can be permitted to be NULL in the relation EMP. Consider the following queries on the database expressed in tuple relational calculus.

Which of the above queries are safe?
questions.solution:
A tuple calculus query is safe if every result value comes from relations in the database. In all three queries, t takes its EmpName from some u in EMP, so the result is finite and drawn from the database in every case. The DEPT conditions only filter.

Answer: (I), (II) and (III)

questions.text:
In a database system, unique time stamps are assigned to each transaction using Lamport's logical clock . Let TS([latex]T_{1}[/latex]) and TS([latex]T_{2}[/latex]) be the timestamps of transactions [latex]T_{1}[/latex] and [latex]T_{2}[/latex] respectively. Besides, [latex]T_{1}[/latex] holds a lock on the resource R, and [latex]T_{2}[/latex] has requested a conflicting lock on the same resource R. The following algorithm is used to prevent deadlocks in the database system assuming that a killed transaction is restarted with the same timestamp.

Assume any transactions that is not killed terminates eventually. Which of the following is TRUE about the database system that uses the above algorithm to prevent deadlocks?
questions.solution:
If the requester T2 is older (smaller timestamp), the younger holder T1 is killed; otherwise the younger requester waits. So a transaction only ever waits for an older one: no cycle of waits [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] deadlock-free.

A killed transaction restarts with its old timestamp, so it keeps getting older relative to new ones and eventually becomes the oldest, which is never killed [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] starvation-free.

Answer: both deadlock-free and starvation-free

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: The database system is both deadlock-free and starvation- free.
The database system is deadlock- free, but not starvation-free.
The database system is starvation-free but not deadlock- free.
The database system is neither deadlock- free nor starvation-free.

questions.text:
Consider the following grammar:

stmt[latex]\rightarrow[/latex] if expr then expr else expr; stmt| [latex]\dot{O}[/latex]
expr[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]term relop term|term
term[latex]\rightarrow[/latex] id|number
if[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]a|b|c
number[latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [0-9]

where relop is a relational operate (e.g [latex]\lt ,\gt[/latex],...), [latex]\dot{O}[/latex] refers to the empty statement, and if ,then, else are terminals.

Consider a program P following the above grammar containing ten if terminals. The number of control flows paths in P is ____________. For example the program

if [latex]e_1[/latex] then [latex]e_2[/latex] else [latex]e_3[/latex]

has 2 controls flow paths [latex]e_{1} \rightarrow e_{2}[/latex] and [latex]e_{1} \rightarrow e_{3}[/latex].
questions.solution:
A program is a sequence of if-then-else statements. Each one has 2 possible branches, and the choices are independent.

With 10 of them: [latex]2^{10}=1024[/latex] control flow paths.

Answer: 1024

questions.text:
In a RSA cryptosystem a participant A uses two prime numbers p=13 and q=17 to generate
her public and private keys. If the public key of A is 35. Then the private key of A is
__________.
questions.solution:
n = 13 [latex]\times[/latex] 17 = 221, [latex]\phi(n)=12\times16=192[/latex]. Private key d satisfies [latex]35d\equiv1\pmod{192}[/latex].

[latex]35\times11=385=2\times192+1[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] d = 11

Answer: 11

questions.text:
The values of parameters for the Stop-and-Wait ARQ protocol are as given below:

Bit rate of the transmission channel = 1Mbps
Propagation delay from sender to receiver = 0.75 ms
Time to process a frame = 0.25ms
Number of bytes in the information frame =1980
Number of bytes in the acknowledge frame = 20
Number of overhead bytes in the information frame = 20

Assume that there are no transmission errors. Then the transmission efficiency ( expressed in percentage) of the Stop-and - Wait ARQ protocol for the above parameters is _________( correct to 2 decimal places)
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Frame transmission: 1980 [latex]\times[/latex] 8 / [latex]10^6[/latex] = 15.84 ms (useful data 1960 bytes = 15.68 ms)
- ACK transmission: 20 [latex]\times[/latex] 8 / [latex]10^6[/latex] = 0.16 ms
- Propagation: 0.75 ms each way; processing 0.25 ms

Cycle = 15.84 + 0.75 + 0.25 + 0.16 + 0.75 = 17.75 ms
Efficiency = 15.68 / 17.75 [latex]\approx[/latex] 88.34%

Answer: 88.34
